chunks: Suleiman ibn Ahmad ibn Ayoob al-Lakhmy narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Abdul Aziz and Mu’az ibn al-Mosana narrated to us, saying: Abdul Salam ibn Salih al-Haravy narrated to us, on the authority of Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha, on the authority of his father Musa, on the authority of his father Ja’far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali, on the authority of his father Ali ibn al-Hussein, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them all), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Faith is knowledge with the heart, verbal affirmation, and action with the pillars (of practice).
ai.seo_question: What are the three essential components of faith in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal articulates the classical Shia definition of Iman as a triad of heart, tongue, and action, distinguishing it from the Murji'ah view that faith is merely internal conviction. It underscores the necessity of integrating theological belief with ritual and practical observance, a cornerstone of Shia jurisprudence. The narration highlights the continuity of this definition through the Imams, linking the Prophet's teaching directly to the Ahl al-Bayt.
